title: Koszul complex of a finite sequence of ring elements
statement: Let $R$ be a commutative ring, $r\ge0$, and $f_1,\dots,f_r\in R$. Let $E=R^{\oplus r}$ be the free $R$-module [def-weil-pbc-free-module] with standard basis $e_1,\dots,e_r$, and $\varphi:E\to R$ the $R$-linear map with $\varphi(e_i)=f_i$. The *Koszul complex* $K_\bullet(f_1,\dots,f_r)=K_\bullet(R,f_1,\dots,f_r)$ is the chain complex of $R$-modules with $K_n=\wedge^n_R E$ (the $n$-th exterior power; $K_0=R$, $K_1=E$, $K_n=0$ for $n>r$ and $n<0$) and differential $d_n:K_n\to K_{n-1}$ the $R$-linear map given on generators by $$d(v_1\wedge\dots\wedge v_n)=\sum_{i=1}^n(-1)^{i+1}\varphi(v_i)\,v_1\wedge\dots\wedge\widehat{v_i}\wedge\dots\wedge v_n\qquad(v_1,\dots,v_n\in E),$$ which is well defined and satisfies $d_{n-1}\circ d_n=0$. Explicitly, $K_n$ is free with basis $e_{i_1}\wedge\dots\wedge e_{i_n}$, $1\le i_1<\dots<i_n\le r$; in low degrees $d_1(e_i)=f_i$ and $d_2(e_i\wedge e_j)=f_ie_j-f_je_i$. For an $R$-module $M$ write $K_\bullet(f_1,\dots,f_r)\otimes_RM$ for the complex with terms $K_n\otimes_RM$ and differentials $d_n\otimes\mathrm{id}_M$, and $H_i(-)=\ker d_i/\operatorname{im}d_{i+1}$ for the homology of a complex.
